About 14–18 million people crossed the borders; death estimates range from 2 lakh to 20 lakh
About 14–18 million people crossed the borders; deaths were uniformly estimated at 2 lakh
Population movement was limited to Punjab and did not affect Bengal
x: An estimated 14–18 million people crossed the borders; death estimates range from 2 lakh to 20 lakh, with many historians near 10 lakh.

s: How many people, mostly kar sevaks, were burnt on the Sabarmati Express near Godhra on 27 February 2002?
x: The Godhra train burning killed 59 people, mostly kar sevaks; a Supreme Court-appointed SIT investigated it.

s: What does ghettoisation following communal riots refer to?
o: temporary migration of workers to industrial areas
legal segregation of citizens by the State
movement of communities into religiously segregated neighbourhoods
division of a district into administrative wards
x: Ghettoisation is the movement of communities into religiously segregated neighbourhoods after communal violence.

s: Which of the following is NOT a consequence of communal violence?
o: Loss of faith in the police and courts
Harm to India's global image and diaspora
x: Communal violence causes polarisation and weakens social capital; it does not strengthen it.

s: About how many people were killed in the 2002 Gujarat riots that followed the Godhra train burning?
x: The riots killed 1,169 people; 59 died in the Sabarmati Express burning itself.

s: About how many people crossed borders during the Partition, the largest forced migration in history?
x: About 14-18 million people crossed borders during Partition.

s: Which body investigated the Godhra and 2002 Gujarat riot cases on the orders of the Supreme Court?
x: The Supreme Court appointed a Special Investigation Team (SIT) to investigate the Godhra and Gujarat riot cases.

s: Which body drafted the Prevention of Communal and Targeted Violence Bill, 2011?
x: The National Advisory Council drafted the Bill, which was never passed.

s: For what purpose were Home Guards first raised in December 1946?
o: help the police control civil disturbance and communal riots
replace the regular police in all districts
x: Home Guards were first raised in December 1946 to assist the police in controlling civil disturbance and communal riots.

s: Who chairs the National Integration Council?
x: The NIC is chaired by the Prime Minister and includes Union ministers, Chief Ministers and eminent persons.

s: The National Foundation for Communal Harmony mainly helps:
x: The National Foundation for Communal Harmony helps child victims and promotes inter-faith dialogue; the Bill was drafted by the National Advisory Council.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about remedies against communal violence?
o: The National Integration Council is chaired by the Prime Minister.
Home Guards were first raised in December 1946.
The Communal and Targeted Violence Bill, 2011 was passed by Parliament.
MHA Guidelines for Communal Harmony cover prevention, containment and response.
x: The Prevention of Communal and Targeted Violence Bill, 2011 was never passed.

s: What did the Sachar Committee (2005) find about Muslims in India?
o: Ahead of other communities in education
Under-represented in public employment, including the police
x: The Sachar Committee found Muslims lagging in education and employment and under-represented in public employment, including the police.

s: Which Supreme Court case directed district nodal officers to prevent mob violence?
o: Prakash Singh v. Union of India (2006)
Ramji Lal Modi v. State of UP
x: Tehseen Poonawalla (2018) directed nodal officers against mob violence; Prakash Singh (2006) dealt with police reforms such as the State Security Commission.

s: Which body is among the police reforms mandated in Prakash Singh v. Union of India (2006)?
x: Prakash Singh (2006) mandated a State Security Commission, Police Establishment Board and Police Complaints Authority.

s: Promoting enmity between groups (IPC 153A) falls under which section of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita?
x: Promoting enmity is BNS 196; BNS 353 (IPC 505) covers statements conducing to public mischief and BNS 299 outraging religious feelings.

s: What range of imprisonment does the Karnataka Hate Speech and Hate Crimes (Prevention) Bill, 2025 provide for?
x: The Bill, described as the first State-level law to define hate speech, provides for two to ten years' imprisonment and covers organisational liability.

s: Which of the following pairs (case – subject) is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Prakash Singh v. Union of India – Police reforms
Pravasi Bhalai Sangathan v. Union of India – Police reforms
Ramji Lal Modi v. State of UP – Validity of Section 295A
Tehseen Poonawalla – Nodal officers for mob violence
x: Pravasi Bhalai Sangathan concerned the request to define hate speech; police reforms came from Prakash Singh.

s: Which of the following is true of 'hate speech' in Indian law?
o: It is defined exclusively by the Supreme Court
It is comprehensively defined in the Constitution
It is defined only in the Indian Penal Code
x: Hate speech is not specifically defined in Indian law.

s: After Pravasi Bhalai Sangathan (2014), which Law Commission report (2017) dealt with defining hate speech?
x: The Supreme Court asked the Law Commission to define hate speech, leading to its 267th Report (2017).

s: Ramji Lal Modi v. State of UP upheld which section of the IPC?
x: Ramji Lal Modi upheld Section 295A (outraging religious feelings), now BNS 299.

s: Which was the first State to bring a law defining hate speech, in 2025?
x: Karnataka's Hate Speech and Hate Crimes (Prevention) Bill, 2025 is the first State law to define hate speech.

s: Under which section of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 is outraging religious feelings (IPC Section 295A) now covered?
x: IPC 295A became BNS Section 299; IPC 153A became BNS 196 and IPC 505 became BNS 353.

s: Under which section of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 are statements conducing to public mischief (IPC Section 505) now covered?
x: IPC 505 became BNS 353; IPC 153A became BNS 196 and IPC 295A became BNS 299.

s: Who began the construction of Mecca Masjid in Hyderabad in 1614?
x: Construction of Mecca Masjid was begun by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah in 1614; it was completed in 1693.

s: Hyderabad's old city saw notable riots in 1978 after which case?
x: The 1978 old-city riots followed the Rameeza Bee case; the Mecca Masjid blast came in 2007.

s: According to the AP Home Department's annual note (January 2026), riots in Andhra Pradesh in 2025:
x: The AP Home Department's annual note (1 Jan 2026) reported that riots in AP fell by 53.88% in 2025. 20.2% is the NCRB conviction rate under Sec. 153A, and 500% is the reported rise in hate-speech cases between 2014 and 2020. 'Rose by 53.88%' reverses the direction.

s: The Mecca Masjid in Hyderabad was completed in 1693 by:
x: Begun in 1614 by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah, the Mecca Masjid was completed in 1693 by Aurangzeb.

s: The bomb blast at Hyderabad's Mecca Masjid took place on:
x: The Mecca Masjid blast occurred on 18 May 2007.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the consequences of regionalism?
o: Balanced development is a negative consequence.
Giving backward regions a voice through regional parties is a positive consequence.
The Tripura TTAADC is cited as an example of intergroup solidarity.
Openings for extremists is a negative consequence.
x: Balanced development is listed as a positive consequence of regionalism, not a negative one.

s: Regional sentiment becomes a negative feature of regional-party politics mainly when it is which of the following?
o: Used to give backward regions a voice
x: Regional feeling turns negative when regional parties exploit it for votes.

s: Several States sharing common interests, as in the North-East, is an example of which type of regionalism?
x: Supra-state regionalism means several States sharing interests; inter-state is conflict between States and intra-state a region within a State seeking recognition.

s: Which of the following defines regionalism?
o: Emotional attachment to a particular area, which may resist a dominant culture or challenge the nation-state
Demand for a separate sovereign country
Devolution of powers to local bodies
Division of a country into administrative zones
x: Regionalism is emotional attachment to a particular area; it may act against cultural dominance or challenge the nation-state.

s: Solidarity through the Tripura Tribal Autonomous District Council is an example of which of the following?
x: It is a positive side of regionalism; negative regionalism includes parochialism and hostility to migrants.

s: In which year was the Dar Commission appointed?
x: The Dar Commission came in 1948, followed by the Visalandhra Mahasabha (1949), Swami Sitaram's fast (1951) and the SRC (1953).

s: What did the Dhar Commission recommend?
o: It rejected language as the basis and preferred administrative convenience.
It recommended the immediate creation of states strictly on a linguistic basis.
It recommended the merger of Andhra State with Telangana.
It recommended the creation of 16 states and 3 territories.
x: The Dhar Commission rejected language as the basis for reorganising provinces and preferred administrative convenience.

s: Who was the Chairman of the States Reorganisation Commission appointed in December 1953?
x: Fazl Ali chaired the SRC; K.M. Panikkar and H.N. Kunzru were its members.

s: How many states and Union Territories did the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 create?
x: The 1956 Act created 14 states and 6 UTs; the SRC (1955) had recommended 16 states and 3 territories.

s: Under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, Andhra State was merged with which region to form Andhra Pradesh?
x: The Act merged Andhra State with Telangana to form Andhra Pradesh, with Hyderabad as capital.

s: Which was the capital of Andhra State, formed on 1 October 1953 as India's first linguistic State?
x: Andhra State was formed on 1 October 1953 with Kurnool as its capital. Hyderabad became the capital only after the 1956 merger with Telangana formed Andhra Pradesh; Guntur and Visakhapatnam were never its capital.

s: Besides Nehru and Patel, who was the third member of the JVP Committee of December 1948?
x: The JVP Committee was Jawaharlal Nehru, Vallabhbhai Patel and Pattabhi Sitaramayya; Panikkar and Kunzru were SRC members.

s: What did the States Reorganisation Commission recommend in its report of September 1955?
x: The SRC recommended 16 states and 3 territories; the SR Act, 1956 created 14 states and 6 UTs.

s: Who was the first to fast unto death for a linguistic State?
x: Potti Sriramulu was the first to fast unto death for a linguistic State; Swami Sitaram fasted in 1951.

s: Who undertook a fast in 1951 for a separate Andhra State?
x: Swami Sitaram fasted in 1951 for Andhra State; Potti Sriramulu later became the first to fast unto death for it.

s: What did the JVP Committee recommend in its report of April 1949?
o: It rejected the linguistic principle for the present, stressing unity and security
It recommended 'one language, one state' for all of India
It recommended 14 states and 6 Union Territories
x: The JVP Committee (Nehru, Patel, Pattabhi Sitaramayya) rejected the linguistic principle for the time being, stressing unity and security.

s: Which was the first ethnic movement in India to win a State?
x: The Andhra Movement was the first ethnic movement to win a State, Andhra State in 1953.

s: Why did B.R. Ambedkar call India a 'Union of States'?
o: Because the States have no right to secede
Because the States were formed by an agreement among themselves
Because each State has its own Constitution
Because the States alone elect the President
x: Ambedkar explained that India is a Union of States because the States have no right to secede from it.

s: Andhra State, formed on 1 October 1953, was carved out of which State?
x: Andhra State was formed by separating the Telugu areas of Madras State; its capital was Kurnool.

s: In which year was the Visalandhra Mahasabha formed?
x: The Visalandhra Mahasabha came in 1949, after the Dhar Commission (1948) and before Swami Sitaram's fast (1951).

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: First linguistic reorganisation commission – Andhra Movement
First new state of the 2000 reorganisation – Chhattisgarh
First major ethnic movement leading to state formation – 7th Constitutional Amendment, 1956
First amendment addressing regional imbalance indirectly – States Reorganisation Commission, 1953
x: Chhattisgarh (1 November 2000) was the first new State of 2000, so this pair is right. The Andhra Movement was the first ethnic movement to win a State, not a commission; the 7th Amendment (1956) came with the States Reorganisation Act and was not an ethnic movement; and the States Reorganisation Commission (1953) was a commission, not an amendment.

s: Which was the first new State formed in 2000?
x: Chhattisgarh (1 Nov 2000) came before Uttarakhand (9 Nov) and Jharkhand (15 Nov).

s: On which date did Telangana become India's 29th State?
x: Telangana was formed from Andhra Pradesh on 2 June 2014 as the 29th State.

s: Which of the following pairs (new State – carved from) is INCORRECTLY matched?
x: Jharkhand was carved out of Bihar, not Madhya Pradesh.

s:
Consider the following statements about pending demands for new States:
1. Vidarbha is a demand from Maharashtra.
2. Gorkhaland concerns the Darjeeling hills of West Bengal.
3. Bundelkhand covers parts of Bihar and Jharkhand.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; Bundelkhand covers parts of Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh.

s:
Arrange the following States in the order of their formation in November 2000:
1. Uttarakhand
2. Jharkhand
3. Chhattisgarh
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Chhattisgarh was formed on 1 November, Uttarakhand on 9 November and Jharkhand on 15 November 2000.

s: The Dravida Nadu demand is an example of which form of regionalism?
x: Dravida Nadu represents secessionism; Telangana represents a demand for a separate State within the Union.

s: Which of the following represents a demand for a new State within the Indian Union rather than secession?
x: Uttarakhand sought a new State within the Union; Dravida Nadu, Khalistan and Greater Nagaland were secessionist demands.

s: Between which States is the Belagavi boundary dispute?
x: Belagavi is the subject of the Maharashtra-Karnataka boundary dispute.

s: Chandigarh is the subject of a capital dispute between which States?
x: Chandigarh is disputed between Punjab and Haryana.

s: With which organisation is the secessionist demand for Greater Nagaland (1980) associated?
x: The Greater Nagaland demand is linked with the NSCN, formed in 1980; it is a secessionist form of regionalism.

s: Which State's 2021 Act reserved 75% of lower-salary private jobs for local candidates?
x: Jharkhand's 2021 Act reserved 75% of lower-salary private jobs; AP's 2019 Act was the first such law and Haryana's came in 2020.

s: The Haryana State Employment of Local Candidates Act, 2020 was struck down in November 2023 by which court?
x: The Punjab and Haryana High Court struck down the Haryana law in November 2023 as unconstitutional.

s: Under Article 16(3) of the Constitution, who alone may prescribe a residence requirement for employment under a State?
x: Article 16(3) allows only Parliament to prescribe a residence requirement (it did so through the Public Employment (Requirement as to Residence) Act, 1957). The State Legislature, Governor and State PSC have no such power; Article 16(2) otherwise bars discrimination by place of birth or residence.

s: Which State passed the first law reserving 75% of private industrial jobs for local candidates, in 2019?

Its main linguistic group, with others treated as outsiders however long they have lived there

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the causes of regionalism?
